p: A developer works on a laptop moving mock UI elements around before typing, which produces an illuminated glowing link icon. The video concludes on an endcard displaying artifactshare.com with the CTA tagline.
Artifact Share simplifies sharing AI generated work with a single updating link instead of manual file exports.

[{"timestamp":"00:00","observation":"Hook text appears over a user dragging a folder icon into a chat box on a laptop."},{"timestamp":"00:03","observation":"Cut to a slightly altered laptop angle where typing spawns an animated glowing link graphic."},{"timestamp":"00:06","observation":"Final CTA screen overlays the domain and value proposition over a dimmed screen."}]

The video conveys the central proposition adequately within the timeframe. Motion is slightly synthetic and AI-generated in appearance around the keyboard interactions, but the text remains readable throughout. Audio effects align cleanly with the visual cues without distortion.

insert into evaluations
           (creative_id, harness_version, hook_score, product_clarity, message_clarity,
            product_salience, cta_intent, visual_quality, artifact_score, overall_score,
            disqualified, failure_modes, critic_notes)
         values (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)
p: The hook line and closing CTA text are legible and on-message, but the on-screen 'product' is a generic abstract dashboard template with colorful blobs and placeholder bars — nothing resembles an actual artifact-sharing UI, comment thread, or live URL until the very last frame's chain-link icon. A developer watching would grasp the pain point (stop exporting/re-sending files) but not what Artifact Share's interface actually looks like or does, which will cap click-through despite the strong hook.
